findings: l.1120-1125 assert without argument that tachyons (space-like, degree 2) are causal. The claim is true. A proof needs an argument the paper does not hint at, because the developed image of such a circle is all of l(p), so no Gamma_p-invariant time function exists on the de Sitter region of e(L). The argument here lifts a CCC to the covering, r -> (s(r), t(r)) with s(r+1) = s(r) + n. If n = 0, dsTime e0 of the developed curve is periodic and monotone, so the curve is constant. If n != 0, the pairing with the null eigenvector e0 + j of Gamma_p is monotone and rescaled by a positive factor at each turn, so it keeps one sign. It is positive above a future time-like direction and negative above a past one, and the developed image contains both. The same argument covers trivial holonomy delta^k and every degree k >= 1.

Stronger than the paper, sorry-free: for every (Gamma_p, l(p))-circle L and every developing data, e(L) has a CCC iff L is Misner (hasCCC_iff_misner). So the two clauses of bbsdef:Hcausal (l.1116) are independent on singular lines. Lines of degree >= 4 (space-like, light-like, trivial holonomy) have no CCC and are excluded only by the degree clause. The « in other words » list (l.1120-1125) is then exactly 'Misner, or degree >= 4' on the CCC side and on the degree side respectively.

kb_proposals: To exclude CCCs where no Gamma_p-invariant time function exists, lift the curve to the covering. GX.GammaLinkCircle.DevData.exists_lift_curve_periodic gives (s, t) with s(r+1) = s(r) + n, and eventually_chart_lift reads every cone chart along it as g . arcPt p (vlift s) t. Then use GX.GammaLinkCircle.DevData.not_hasCCC_of_future_past, which needs only a future and a past time-like direction in the developed image.
The regular part of BiSusp S is homeomorphic to S x ]0, pi[ through GX.BiSusp.regHomeo (mk' on regSet univ). It gives continuous coordinates (sigma, t) of any curve that avoids the poles.
On a single e(L) the CCC question is settled: GX.GammaLinkCircle.DevData.hasCCC_iff_misner, sorry-free.
